_why: Issue #120 lets a row set its collection's summary and sort title. Five things about Plex decide how
that has to be written, and none of them was recorded, so they were measured on a throwaway
collection before any code was written (unmarked, no shortlist_* label, deleted in a finally).
1. A LOCKED titleSort survives a title edit and a membership write. So a row that is renamed (or a
{top_seed} row, which renames itself) keeps its OLD sort title until Shortlist writes the new one.
2. An UNLOCKED custom titleSort is overwritten by the next title edit. So Shortlist must lock it.
3. Blanking and unlocking titleSort makes Plex rebuild it from the FULL title, leading emoji kept.
Plex's own derivation (on create, and on every later title edit) drops the leading emoji. So a
revert that sends no title leaves `✨ X` sorting as `✨ X` until the row's next rename. The revert
deliberately does NOT re-send the title to get the canonical form: rows are found by title, and
the title a plexapi object holds is stale after a rename, so re-sending it could undo one.
4. The summary is stored byte-exact — newline, trailing spaces, '&', '<' and emoji all round-trip —
so comparing Plex's value with the wanted one before writing is safe.
5. A field edit leaves labels alone, and costs ~0.01-0.09s even on this server's slowest library,
where a label write took 21.9s and a membership write 17.1s. Both fields go in ONE PUT.
library: TV Shows (4,980 shows, ~120k episodes — the library every membership write is slow on)
